tables: RESULTS.md (A1 trajectory, A2 variables, A3 newcomer benchmark, A4 sister channel, B packaging facts)
verdict: FLAT. The channel ramped from 53 to ~1.1K views per Short in the first ~10 h (uploads 1 to 3) and has sat at that level since (788 / 1,174, plus one throttled outlier at <85). ~1.2-1.4K is the default first-test audience for new channels (p75 at every upload index 1-10 in a 144-channel sample). The hook metric (stayed) has not improved: 57.6, 62.6, 42.8, 54.1, 39.5 %. The body metrics have (AVP 53 to 81 %).

findings.claim: The trajectory is a ramp followed by a plateau, not a rise. Views in the first ~10 h went 53 > 286 > 1,101 > 788 > <85 > 1,174. No Short has passed 2,312. The channel reached the new-channel first-test ceiling at upload #3 and has stayed there.
findings.evidence: trajectory.json (per_video daily + summary.json + Studio points from memory atlas-ape-retention.md); newcomers_stats.json: p75 views by upload index 1-10 = 1,282/1,195/1,195/1,255/1,232/1,187/1,253/1,438/1,313/1,194 (144 new channels)
findings.action: Stop reading 'more views than last time' as progress. The only milestone that matters next is the first Short past ~10K. Judge each Short on its Studio stayed % at 24 h and on its views at 7 days.

findings.claim: The hook is the bottleneck, and it is not improving across iterations. It sits well below the level that took a benchmark channel past its first test.
findings.evidence: Studio stayed %: 57.6 / 62.6 / 42.8 / 54.1 / 39.5 (memory atlas-ape-retention.md, atlas-ape-channel.md). Relative retention vs same-length Shorts at 10-30 % of the video: 0.29 / 0.26 / 0.49 / 0.42, i.e. below the median (trajectory.json from per_video.json). Isaac's benchmark: 60.1 % stayed > 1,080 views at 24 h, 59.1 % > 1,144, 79.6 % > 21.4K (memory isaac-7day-experiment.md).
findings.action: Gate every upload on its first 3 s. Read stayed % at 24 h and treat <70 % as a hook fail. Run the planned A/B (same script, two openings) instead of changing the whole video.

findings.claim: Shortening worked for the body and ending. For the 4 Shorts with Analytics, the views ranking follows AVP and shortness, not stayed %. Yellow Fleet has the lowest stayed and the most views.
findings.evidence: AVP 53.1 / 45.3 / 81.3 / 70.4. End retention 26.7 / 15.3 / 46.5 / 37.9 %. Relative retention in the last 20 %: 0.50 / 0.57 / 0.79 / 0.61. Views 663 / 1,154 / 2,312 / 1,407 (trajectory.json). N=4, so this is a hypothesis.
findings.action: Keep 30-45 s single-arc scripts with a short tail. Put the effort into the first 3 s, not the middle.

findings.claim: Only Yellow Fleet got a real delayed second wave. Pig War's 'extra' views were the first wave running past the PT-midnight cutoff of Analytics. Rabbits and Volcano have stopped.
findings.evidence: YF: 1,101 (PT day 1) + 67 (day 2) = 1,168, then 2,312 by 83 h (+1,144, +98 %). Pig War: 788 @ 9.8 h, 1.2K @ 14 h, 1,407 @ 58.6 h (~4.7/h tail). Rabbits: 286/409/455 per day, then +4 since 22.10. Volcano: +1 since 22.10. Sources: per_video.json, raw/fresh_counts_*.json.
findings.action: Check Studio traffic sources for YF on 23-25.10 to see which surface retested it. Do not delete or re-upload old Shorts.

findings.claim: Farm girl was held back from the start. It never got the ~1K first test, while Yellow Fleet, with a similar stayed %, did. Audience rejection alone does not explain this.
findings.evidence: Farm girl: 85 @ 18 h, 125-132 @ 33 h (raw/fresh_counts_*.json; videos_B/repull) and stayed 39.5 %. YF: 42.8 % stayed and 1,101 views in 10.7 h. API shows no regionRestriction (raw/videos_localizations.json). The video contains Confused Travolta / Stonks / CJ clips plus Flow/Veo AI frames (memory ai-farm-girl-short.md).
findings.action: Owner: open Studio > Content > Restrictions / Copyright for 06A_mm0ZkGw and report any claim or limited status. Until that is known, no copyrighted meme clips.

findings.claim: Uploads #5 and #6 changed the execution numbers a lot, toward the viral medians. The results have not improved yet: farm girl is the worst, and Russell is on the same ~1.17K first test.
findings.evidence: Motion in second 0-1: 4.04 / 1.90 / 0.72 / 1.08 > 13.47 / 19.61. Words/s: 2.01 / 1.93 / 2.65 / 2.34 > 3.31 / 3.08. Russell's first cut at 2.67 s (../videos_A/measure_*.json, ../videos_B/measure_*.json). Russell: 1,174 views from 07:45 to 08:02 UTC, unchanged across 5 polls (raw/fresh_counts_*.json, videos_B/repull).
findings.action: Get Russell's Studio stayed % and swiped % at 24 h, and its views at 7 days, before calling the new rules a success or a failure. N=2.

findings.claim: People who watch like it about as much as viewers of the owner's successful German channel like that channel. What is missing is sharing and comments.
findings.evidence: Likes/1k views: ATLAS 15.4 (Pig War 25.6, Russell 20.4) vs WWW Oct 11.7 and WWW first 6 Shorts 18.2. Subs per 1k views: 0.76 vs 0.96. Comments/1k: 0.44 vs 1.19. Shares: 0 on all 3,768 Analytics views (summary.json, sharing.json, raw/wwm_api.json).
findings.action: Build one share trigger into each script (a 'send this to…' absurd fact) and pin a question comment within the first hour.

findings.claim: Base rates for new channels in this niche: about 1 in 10 gets a 10K Short in its first 6 uploads, and about 1 in 80 gets a 1M in its first 10. ATLAS APE is above most newcomers but not in the group that breaks out. Breakouts mostly come early.
findings.evidence: 188 new channels (first upload on or after 1.7.2026, search order=date, Shorts ≥7 d old): any of first 6 ≥10K = 10.1 % (English 8.4 %); any of first 10 ≥1M = 1.6 % (English 1.2 %); median Short 266 views. Ours: median 1,164 = 78th-80th percentile; best 2,312 = 84th-87th. Of 35 channels that looked like us after 6 Shorts, 2 (5.7 %) passed 10K in Shorts 7-10. First ≥10K came by Short #3 for 13 of 18 channels that broke out (newcomers_stats.json).
findings.action: Set the next target to one Short ≥10K, not 1M. More uploads of the same thing has ~6 % odds over the next 4, so change the opening and format, not the volume alone.

findings.claim: The owner's own German channel shows what reach looks like with a format that fits its market. Its first 6 Shorts did 57 times better than ATLAS APE's, with longer videos. Viewers react similarly once they watch, so the gap is distribution: market plus one consistent topic and format.
findings.evidence: WWW first 6 Shorts (May 2026): 20.5K-88.3K, median 66,897, 52 s. 8-24.10: 29 Shorts, median 87,583, min 17,623, max 511,336, 68 s, 2 uploads/day. 4,240 subs, 4.40M views. German WW2 / tank / map what-ifs with question titles (raw/wwm_api.json). ATLAS APE median 1,164.
findings.action: Run a controlled test: 2-3 ATLAS APE Shorts built on WWW's proven structure (question title, animated-map paradox, one topic family, same look) in English. That shows whether the English market or the format is the wall.

findings.claim: Each upload changed 4-6 variables at once, so the data cannot say what helped.
findings.evidence: Length 77 > 63 > 33 > 42 > 33 > 44 s. Look: real-DEM 3D > toy 3D > Blender toy > drawn + Flow AI > Flow/Veo + memes > drawn in code. Atlas role: host > hook/end > friend > ending > pop-ins > removed. VO went from the free key to the paid key, and the hook rules changed (RESULTS.md A2).
findings.action: Freeze the format for the next 6 uploads and change one variable per pair, using the owner's R2 A/B rule.

findings.claim: Several key data points are still missing, so all causal reads are hypotheses.
findings.evidence: N=6. Analytics only covers PT days through 22.10: no rows for #5/#6, Pig War only 9.8 h. Stayed % comes from Studio screenshots only. The comments API is not in token scope. subscribedStatus returns a 500 error (subscribed_status.json). Russell is 10 h old.
findings.action: Re-run pull.py on 28.10. The owner should send Studio stayed/swiped % for Russell (24 h) and for farm girl and Russell at 7 days.

findings.claim: The first-test audience is global and mostly Asian outside the US. It is adult men, all new viewers, almost all from the feed.
findings.evidence: Channel to 22.10: US 24.3 %, PH 15.3 %, IN 5.3 %, ID 4.6 %, MY 3.4 %. Male 75.1 %, age 25-44 60.6 %, 13-17 11.8 %. Mobile 80 %, tablet 13 % (country_channel.json, demographics.json, device.json). Rabbits' seed was 30 % PH.
findings.action: No action. This is the normal seed pool. Don't tailor content to PH/IN.

findings.claim: Packaging (title, description, channel page) touches at most ~3 % of current views. It cannot explain the plateau. The feed swipe happens on the first 1-2 s of video, before anyone reads a title.
findings.evidence: traffic_channel.json: Shorts feed 3,664 / 3,768 = 97.2 %, search 1.5 %, other page 0.6 %, subscriber 0.3 %, channel page 0.3 %.
findings.action: Fix the cheap packaging items once, in about 30 min total, then spend the time on frames 0-3 s. Packaging starts to matter after a breakout, when people land on the channel page.

findings.claim: In all 4 uploads that had a title kit, the uploaded title differed from the kit. Every emoji was dropped and 2 titles were replaced. Russell's uploaded title drops the proven same-story keyword and previews part of the twist.
findings.evidence: Kits: YF '…8 YEARS 🚢 · 11.ai', uploaded with a double space where the emoji was. Pig War 'Britain Lost an Island Because of a PIG 🐷🇬🇧', uploaded with alternative 1. Farm girl '… Her 💔'. Russell 'He Escaped Prison 4 Times Without Breaking a Lock 😳' (same-story Short 'He Escaped From Prison 4 Times 😧' = 1.06M), uploaded as 'He Escaped Prison Dressed as a Doctor', while the VO twist is 'Posing as a doctor…' (videos.json, UPLOAD.md / YOUTUBE.md files). Title sample, channels <1M subs: 42 % of ≥1M titles have an emoji vs 18 % of <100K titles; median 7 vs 10 words (titles_stats.py). This is a correlation.
findings.action: Upload kit titles as written, or say why not. Swap Russell to the kit title after 48 h, as the kit planned.

findings.claim: The ' · 11.ai' suffix on titles 1-3 is required by the free ElevenLabs licence, so it cannot be removed without re-voicing. To viewers it reads as an AI-tool watermark. No winning title in the sample carries a tool credit.
findings.evidence: memory elevenlabs-free-plan.md. In the 482-Short sample, ' | ' / ' · ' separators in ≥1M titles are series or brand names ('| Prison Break S1E10'), never tool credits (titles_stats.py output). Uploads #4-#6 have no suffix (paid key since 22.10).
findings.action: Already fixed going forward. Never publish free-key VO again. Leave the 3 old titles; their distribution has ended.

findings.claim: The channel page gives no reason to subscribe, and its promise contradicts the content.
findings.evidence: channel.json: description '' (flagged 21.10, draft ready in ~/shorts/orang-branding/out/channel_description_v2.txt), no keywords (brandingSettings has title+country only), 0 user playlists (raw/playlists_mine.json), 0 channel sections (raw/channel_sections.json). Banner (orang-branding/out/banner.png): 'The whole world on my shoulders — explained · GEOGRAPHY · MAPS · FACTS', but 6/6 videos are absurd true stories. Name used four ways: ATLAS APE / THE ATLAS APE / The Atlas Ape / @atlasape-s. 4 subs from 5,239 views.
findings.action: Today: paste the v2 description and keywords, change the banner tagline to the story promise ('Weird history and true stories so absurd they sound made up'), add one playlist, and use one spelling of the name.

findings.claim: The mascot is not working as a brand. Atlas's screen role shrank with every upload and he was removed from Russell. The channel is named after a character viewers barely see. There is also no series name to promise a format.
findings.evidence: Volcano host lip-sync > Rabbits hook/key/end > YF friend lip-sync > Pig War ending only > farm girl pop-ins > Russell removed (project STATUS.md files, memory conman-russell-short.md). WWW's channel name is itself the format promise ('Was wäre wenn').
findings.action: Decide one of two: (a) Atlas becomes a fixed 1-2 s signature in every Short (same pose and spot, e.g. the final reaction that loops), or (b) the brand promise moves to the story format, not the ape.

findings.claim: YouTube classifies each Short differently. Yellow Fleet was tagged as video-game content, and its only demographic bucket above the reporting threshold is boys 13-17. That points to the toy-3D look being read as gaming.
findings.evidence: videos.json topicDetails: Volcano and Rabbits 'Knowledge', YF 'Video_game_culture', Pig War 'Entertainment/Film/Politics', farm girl 'Entertainment', Russell none yet. per_video.json YF demographics: male 13-17 = 100 % (thresholded). Category 27 on all.
findings.action: Use one look and one topic family for the next 10 Shorts so the algorithm can build an audience model. This is a hypothesis, N=1.

findings.claim: The prepared title and description translations were never added. Every video has only 'en' localizations.
findings.evidence: raw/videos_localizations.json: localizations = ['en'] on all 6. Kits for Russell, Pig War and farm girl contain ES / PT-BR / FR / DE versions.
findings.action: Add them (about 5 min per video). The effect on reach is unproven.

findings.claim: Upload time is not a lever at 4 subscribers. Cadence is 1 per day vs 2 per day on WWW, and one finished Short is sitting unpublished.
findings.evidence: Uploads at 20:08-22:28 UTC = 13:08-15:28 PT, one per day 19-24.10 (summary.json). WWW uploads 2/day at 04:55-17:30 UTC (raw/wwm_api.json). football-222 is built and not uploaded.
findings.action: Publish football-222 and keep at least 1 per day. Don't tune the clock.

findings.claim: Upload hygiene is correct.
findings.evidence: madeForKids false, defaultLanguage/defaultAudioLanguage 'en', captions true, category 27 consistent, sourced descriptions, no region restrictions (videos.json). Custom cover only on 3/6: Rabbits, Pig War, Russell.
findings.action: Set a cover frame on every upload. It is shown on search and channel-page shelves.
